findings.title: isAccessTokenId() matcher has inverted logic and off-by-one substring indices
Constructor validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId
New abstract method getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` is a provider factory interface that custom/extension grant-type providers can implement. This PR adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut();` with no default implementation. Any existing third-party implementation of this interface (compiled against the previous version, or even recompiled without updating) will fail to compile or throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime, because the interface contract has changed without providing backward compatibility (e.g. a default method returning a fallback shortcut). This is a breaking API/contract change for anyone extending this SPI.

findings.title: Removed public copy constructor from OAuth2GrantType.Context without deprecation
findings.body: The public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` was removed from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`. This is a public API that any custom `OAuth2GrantType`/`OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementation might rely on to clone/wrap a Context object (e.g. to adjust grant type before delegating). Removing it outright, rather than deprecating first, is a binary/source compatibility break for any external code using this constructor.

findings.title: Potential NullPointerException if cache-miss fallback runs before postInit() populates sessionFactory
findings.body:
`getGrantTypeByShortcut()` (and similarly `getShortcutByGrantType()` at line 110) dereferences `sessionFactory` directly in the fallback branch used when a shortcut/grant type isn't found in the cached maps:
```
sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(OAuth2GrantType.class) ...
```
`sessionFactory` is only assigned inside `postInit()`. If this provider's methods are invoked (by this factory or any other SPI) before `postInit()` runs, or if `create()`/the provider instance is otherwise used prior to full lifecycle completion, this throws an unguarded NPE instead of gracefully returning null/unknown. There is no null-check or lazy-initialization guard protecting this access.

findings.title: Test catches overly broad RuntimeException, masking an unrelated NPE instead of verifying intended IllegalArgumentException
findings.body: `testIncorrectGrantType()` builds a `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` by calling only `init(null)` and manually populating `grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts`, without ever calling `postInit()`. This leaves the factory's `sessionFactory` field null. The test then calls `provider.getTokenContextFromTokenId("ofrtac:5678")` with grant shortcut `ac` absent from the stub map, which triggers `getGrantTypeByShortcut()`'s fallback branch that dereferences the null `sessionFactory`, throwing a `NullPointerException` rather than the intended `IllegalArgumentException` for an unrecognized grant shortcut. Because the test catches the overly broad `RuntimeException`, it passes regardless of which exception is actually thrown, so it does not verify the intended validation behavior and would silently continue to pass even if the real `IllegalArgumentException` path were broken.

findings.title: Access token id format change (non-UUID prefix) has no migration/compat notes and may break consumers assuming UUID-formatted token ids
findings.body: `initToken()` now sets the access token's `id` (the `jti` claim) to an encoded value like `onrtac:1f65761e-...` rather than a plain UUID produced by `KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()`. This changes the format/contract of the access token id for all tokens going forward. The PR itself had to update `AssertEvents` test matchers (replacing `isUUID()` checks on `TOKEN_ID` details with a new matcher) because of this format change, demonstrating that other code paths, external integrations, logging/analytics tooling, or custom extensions that assume access token ids are plain 36-character UUIDs (e.g. any `UUID.fromString()` parsing, fixed-length storage, or string-length assumptions) could break. No changelog/upgrade-guide note or compatibility discussion is included for this change in token id semantics.
